scalars.scalar_value: Three (3) years of formal experience, training, internship, or leadership experience reasonably related to this management assignment.

items.item_text: Must possess and maintain a valid Class C driver’s license during the course of employment.
Three (3) years of formal experience, training, internship, or leadership experience reasonably related to this management assignment.
Oversees, manages, and plans the daily functions, operations, and activities of District Learning Centers. (E)
Provides administrative and professional leadership and direction for District Learning Centers. (E)

Leads in developing strategic plans for the program by coordinating with other departments and divisions; works with faculty and various disciplines to increase effectiveness and programs, services, and activities offerings. (E)
Promotes diversity, equity, inclusion, cultural competency, and a positive work and academic environment. (E)
Administers, develops, and implements goals, objectives, policies, procedures, work standards, and internal controls for the department and assigned program areas. (E)
Works in concert with faculty and staff to manage an inclusive and integrated Learning Center. (E)

Administers, develops, and standardizes procedures and methods to improve and continuously monitor the efficiency and effectiveness of assigned programs, service delivery methods, and procedures; assesses and monitors workload, administrative and support systems, and internal reporting relationships; identifies opportunities for improvement and makes recommendations to the Dean. (E)
Develops, analyzes, and implements pedagogical strategies for students, faculty, and staff. (E)
Directs and develops an outreach program to promote Learning Center activities and offerings. (E)
Serves as the liaison between Deans, Counselors, and faculty in enhancing the retention of target students. (E)
Coordinates with faculty, and dean to lead in the development, review and implementation of curriculum and program review. (E)
Hires, supervises, trains, motivates, and evaluates the Learning Center faculty, staff, tutors, and student workers. (E)
Establishes academic and work schedules and faculty assignments in coordination with division dean and faculty. (E)
Plans and conducts research designed to facilitate a culture of data-driven decision making within the area, with the Director of Institutional Research and Planning. (E)
Ensures equitable and appropriate services are provided to students in culturally relevant approaches.
Provides leadership for data-informed discussions and implementation of program improvements and analyzes the effectiveness of Learning Center services. (E)
Gathers and analyzes data and leads discussions regarding program needs with the Research Office and Enrollment Services. (E)
Participates in participatory governance of the institution and fosters an environment of collegiality. (E)
Prepares, administers and monitors assigned budgets; allocates resources in a cost-effective manner. (E)
Provides regular updates to the supervising Dean regarding student success data and Learning Center activities. (E)

Continues to build knowledge of current trends in academic support services and effective practices by visiting other colleges, attending workshops and state and national conferences, reading professional journals, analyzing research reports, and connecting through listservs. (E)
Monitors changes in laws, regulations, and technology that may affect District or departmental operations; implements policy and procedural changes as required. (E)
Responds to difficult and sensitive public inquiries and complaints and assists with resolutions and alternative recommendations. (E)
Learns and applies emerging technologies and software and, as necessary, to perform duties in an efficient, organized, and timely manner. (E)
Participates in the educational mission of the District. (E)
Performs other related duties as assigned.
Course work in Business Administration, Mathematics, English or related field.
Equity-based principles and leadership in higher education.
Effective oral, written, and electronic communications.
Evidence of effective planning in the management, supervision, and evaluation of the work of others.
An understanding of how technology can support learning and a record of support for technological advancements.
Administrative principles and practices, including goal setting, program development, implementation, and evaluation.
Budget development, administrative practices, and organizational and management practices as applied to the analysis and evaluation of projects, programs, policies, procedures, and operational needs.
Principles and practices of employee supervision, including work planning, assignment, review and evaluation, and the training of staff in work procedures.
Principles and practices of developing, implementing, and evaluating learning center programs, services, and activities.
Applicable Federal, State, and local laws, regulatory codes, ordinances, and procedures relevant to assigned programs, projects, and operations.
Methods and techniques for the development of presentations, business correspondence, and information distribution; research and reporting methods, techniques, and procedures.
Principles and procedures of record keeping.
Modern office practices, methods, and computer equipment and applications.

Techniques for effectively representing the District in contacts with governmental agencies, community groups, and various business, professional, educational, regulatory, and legislative organizations.

Techniques for providing a high level of customer service by effectively dealing with the public, vendors, students, and District staff, including individuals of various ages, disabilities, socio-economic and ethnic groups.
Plan, organize, develop, and evaluate the programs, and activities of the Learning Center.
Interpret, apply, and explain rules, regulations, requirements, and restrictions.
Organize work and meet schedules and deadlines.
Evaluate faculty and staff with recommendations for program improvements and/or new services.
Supervise both weekend and evening employees in the Learning Center.
Travel between campuses and centers.
Develop and implement goals, objectives, policies, procedures, work standards, and internal controls for the department and assigned areas.
Provide administrative and professional leadership and direction for the department.
Prepare and administer budgets; allocate limited resources in a cost-effective manner.
Plan, organize, direct, and coordinate the work of professional and technical personnel; delegate authority and responsibility.
Select, train, motivate, and evaluate the work of staff and train staff in work procedures.
Research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods, procedures, and techniques.
Effectively administer a variety of learning center programs, services, and activities.
Effectively represent the department in meetings with various educational, business, professional, regulatory, and legislative organizations.
Prepare clear and concise reports, correspondence, policies, procedures, and other written materials.
Conduct complex research projects, evaluate alternatives, make sound recommendations, and prepare effective technical staff reports.
Establish and maintain a variety of filing, record keeping, and tracking systems.
Organize and prioritize a variety of projects and multiple tasks in an effective and timely manner; organize own work, set priorities, and meet critical time deadlines.
Understand scope of authority in making independent decisions.
Review situations accurately and determine appropriate course of action using judgment according to established policies and procedures.
Establish, maintain, and foster positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
Demonstrate knowledge and evidence of student support programs.
Collaborative team building skills.
Operate office equipment including computer equipment and specialized software applications programs.
Use English effectively to communicate in person, over the telephone, and in writing.

Demonstrate a sensitivity to, and understanding of, the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students.
